findings.title: Coworkers only react when something is counted as 'broken', so every reaction costs damage, money and the 'Break nothing' bonus
findings.room: all floor rooms + lobby (playground, meeting, lunch, lobby, arcade, qfn)
findings.problem: The world reacts to Pip's chaos in exactly one place. `alarm()` is called from the prop-impact branch in src/game.ts:335, and that branch also sets `prop.damaged=true`, `damage++` and `cost+=prefab.cost`. Startling a coworker and breaking a prop are the same event: you can't get the '!' bubble without a damage point and a cost. A thrown bin that lands upright next to the trainee (world-reacts-01) shows no crack, dent or spilt contents, yet the HUD jumps to damage 1 / cost 8, and the Playground's 'Break nothing' star (src/ui/objectives.ts:30) goes dark in the same frame. The same happens with the Lobby chair (damage 1, cost 25, world-reacts-02), the Meeting plant (damage 1, cost 15, world-reacts-03), the Lunch mop (damage 1, cost 5, world-reacts-05), the QFN cart (damage 1, cost 50) and the Arcade mug (damage 1, cost 5). For the player, the slapstick that should be free play (DR-03/DR-04) is silently charged as wrecking. There is no visual sign of what was 'broken', so the grade feels arbitrary. Every throw at a desk also takes a step toward losing 'Break fewer than 5 things' (objectives.ts:38). This conflates DR-04 (the world reacts) with DR-07 (the damage axis), and it works against AGENTS 5 (chaos second, never punished as a fail) in spirit.
findings.fix: Split the impact branch at src/game.ts:335 into two tiers. (1) Impact: lastSpeed>4 and a deceleration >3. Call `this.alarm(pos,3.5)`, play the thud or clatter and the dust, and do not touch damage or cost. Allow it again after a 1 s per-prop cooldown, rather than once per prop forever. (2) Break: only for fragile kinds (add `fragile:true` to glass, monitor, mug, plant, printer and coffee in src/props/prefabs.ts), or any kind at lastSpeed>9. This tier sets `damaged`, counts damage and cost, and shows a visible state: swap in a cracked or tilted variant mesh, or a lid-off/soil-spill decal, so the player can see what they paid for.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/throw.mjs playground 6 throw 01. Expect alarmed ≥1 at +0.5 s with damage 0 and cost 0 for the bin, and the 'Break nothing' star still lit in world-reacts-01-…-react.png. Throwing a mug at a wall still counts 1 damage and shows a broken-mug mesh.
findings.verify_reason: The only alarm() call on an impact is inside the damage branch at src/game.ts:335 (prop.damaged=true; damage++; cost+=). I reproduced it: I threw a bin at the playground trainee, and at +0.7 s alarmed went to 1 in the same tick that damage went 0→1 and cost 0→8. The HUD shows 1 / 8 and the bin sits upright and undamaged beside the trainee. In the Meeting, a plain sprint also counted one chair as broken (cost 25, alarmed 4). 'Break nothing' is defined at src/ui/objectives.ts:30 as damage===0, so one throw kills it.

findings.title: No funny or physical moment within 30 s on any clean route: zero props move, and nobody reacts to Pip
findings.problem: I replayed each room's clean spec route in 1 m steps (tools/world-reacts/clean.mjs) and logged fastestProp, alarmed and the effects at each step. Playground: fastestProp is 0.0 for the whole run and alarmed is 0. The only beats are the plug-in flash at 8.6 s and the win confetti at about 9.5 s, and Pip passes the trainee at (−6.6,−3.4) without a glance. Meeting: within 30 s the only thing is the cyan ring when the strip snaps (10.8 s). The first coworker alarm comes at 64.4 s, from the taut-cable proximity alarm, and the first spark at about 80 s (strip trip). Lunch: wedge, mop and drop, then the kitchen plug spark at 33.9 s, past the 30 s line. alarmed stays 0 and no prop moves faster than walking speed. DR-16's clear 1.2 m lanes (src/levels/playground.ts:6 `lanes`) do their job, but they also guarantee that the tidy player never bumps into anything. Coworkers' only response to Pip passing within 2 m is a 12% squash (`near` → duck .88, src/game.ts:426), which can't be seen at the game camera. A player who follows the card gets a quiet, comedy-free first half-minute in every floor room, which breaks DR-03.
findings.fix: Seed 2–3 'gag props' on the edge of each clean lane, inside the first 10–15 s of walking. Examples: a wobbly paper tower or a cone that tips when Pip passes within 0.6 m; a swivel chair that spins away (apply a 1.5 N·s angular impulse when Pip's capsule touches it); at Meeting, the printer spitting a sheet when the strip is lifted off its stand (−8.6,−3.2). Make coworkers react to Pip himself: in the npc loop (src/game.ts:423), when d<1.4 and Pip's pace >5.5 (sprint), set npc.alarm=.6 and play voice('alarm'); when Pip walks past slowly, play a short 'hm' with a head-turn. In Lunch, add a corridor bot whose painted loop crosses the power-room door in the first 10 s so it bumps Pip or the thick dolly.
findings.verify: Rerun `node mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/clean.mjs playground|meeting|lunch`. The log must show a row with t<30 that has alarmed>0, or a non-held prop with fast>3, and a screenshot at that time must show the bubble or the gag prop in motion.
findings.verify_reason: The code supports it. A nearby coworker only gets duck .88 (src/game.ts:426). plugFlash (src/game.ts:249) never calls alarm. The Meeting and Lunch clean routes have no gag props. I did not rerun clean.mjs, so the per-step log is unverified. Caveat: in ?manual mode, frame() still calls render(dt) with real rAF time (src/game.ts:454-459), so npc.alarm decays in wall-clock time. A short alarm between log rows can therefore be missed, and 'alarmed 0 for the whole run' is weaker evidence than it looks. In the Playground the clean player does get a plug-in hit-stop, a spark/star/shockwave and win confetti inside about 10 s, which arguably counts as 'physical'. The finding holds firmly for Meeting and Lunch, and is weaker for Playground.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:454-459 (alarm decays in real time even in manual mode)
src/game.ts:465 (advance renders only once at the end)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the gag props out of the 1.2 m clean lanes (DR-16) and make them non-damaging: do not route them through the damage branch at game.ts:335. Otherwise the clean player loses 'Break nothing' just for walking by. Instrument the verify with a beats log (see finding 13), not by polling alarmed.

findings.title: Meeting's glass wall can't be smashed: thrown props, sprinting and even throwing the pane leave it intact, and a sprint silently slides it open
findings.problem: The documented Meeting chaos route is 'smash the glass wall (big cost) to shorten the route' (docs/LEVEL_01_BIG_MEETING.md:21). I tried three ways. (1) A bin thrown at the pane at (9.3,−6.1): the bin counts as broken (damage 1) and two boardroom blobs startle, but all three panes stay `enabled` and undamaged (world-reacts-17). (2) A 1.2 s sprint into the pane: no smash, damage 0, alarmed 0. Instead the 2.6 m pane slides 1.1 m into the boardroom (glass-0 x 9.3→10.39, glass-1 →10.5) and Pip walks in through the gap (world-reacts-18). The shortcut opens for free and without a sound. (3) Grabbing the pane (prompt 'E Grab the thing') and throwing it with Q: it topples onto Pip intact, damage 0 (world-reacts-22, -23). Glass only breaks when the pane's own lastSpeed exceeds 5.5 and it then decelerates (src/game.ts:335), which a 7 kg pane (src/props/prefabs.ts:17) never reaches from these actions. The most Good Job–like gag in the room (the research doc cites reviewers 'giggling … launching workers through glass windows', docs/RESEARCH_good_job_nintendo.md:42) never fires. The free slide also hands the chaos player the shortcut at no cost, which skips the risk/reward the doc intends.
findings.fix: Make glass panes Fixed bodies (not dynamic or grabbable) until they break. Turn on Rapier contact-force events on the glass colliders (`ActiveEvents.CONTACT_FORCE_EVENTS`, with a threshold of about 40 N). Break the pane when any dynamic prop hits it above 3 m/s relative speed, when Pip touches it at sprint pace (>5.5), or when a slingshot impulse passes within 1.1 m. On break, call `consume`, emit the existing 14-shard burst and `audio.glass()`, call `alarm(pos,5)`, and add the 250 cost. Leave a shard decal on the floor. Exclude 'glass' from nearest() so the 'Grab the thing' prompt disappears.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/chaos.mjs meeting. The thrown bin, or the sprint, must disable at least one glass-N, raise cost by 250 and set alarmed ≥2. The pane must not slide (x stays 9.3 ±0.05). Retake world-reacts-17/-18 to show shards and bubbles.
findings.verify_reason: The glass panes are ordinary dynamic props (addProp uses RigidBodyDesc.dynamic, src/game.ts:122; glass mass 7, src/props/prefabs.ts:17). They only break through the generic lastSpeed>5.5 branch at src/game.ts:335. I reproduced the sprint myself: a 1.2 s sprint from (7.2,-5.6) pushed glass-1 from x 9.3 to 10.53, Pip ended up inside the boardroom at (10.15,-6.39), and every pane stayed enabled with damaged=false. The prompt still reads 'E Grab the thing' next to the pane. The doc's chaos route says to smash the glass wall (docs/LEVEL_01_BIG_MEETING.md:21), and that never happens.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap6-world-reacts-05-meet-glass-sprint.jpg (Pip through the gap, panes intact, 'Grab the thing')
v.mjs meet log: after sprint glass-1 x 10.53, en true, dmg false
findings.fix_correction: Make the panes Fixed, as the finding says. Rather than relying on Rapier contact-force events alone, which need an extra event queue drained in step(), the simplest change is a per-step check in step(): break the pane when any enabled dynamic prop with speed>3 is within its AABB plus 0.15 m, or when Pip's pace>5.5 within 0.6 m. Note the pace check is computed at src/game.ts:319. Keep the cost at 250 as the doc's 'big cost'.

findings.title: Lunch's cables are too long to slingshot anywhere near the crowd, so the room's coworkers can never be hit by cable chaos
findings.problem: The thin leads are 32/30/32 m and the thick lead 30 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61), in a 32 × 20 m floor. I picked up thin-1 at Supply A (−10.8,2), walked past the corridor crowd at (−3.8,9) and (−2.4,8.9), then sprinted east for 2 s. Strain only reached 0.77, with Pip at (10.8,5.9), the far side of the room (world-reacts-14). Q then just drops the end: release() only slingshots at energy>1 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:199-201), so alarmed stays 0, fastestProp is 0 and nothing flies (world-reacts-15). Sprinting with a live cable right past three seated coworkers drew no reaction either, because the taut-cable proximity alarm (src/game.ts:301) needs strain >0.9 and only runs for the main rope, not Lunch's cables. Lunch is the room with the biggest audience (9 blobs, a corridor queue), yet the signature act (AGENTS 4, DR-06) can't reach them, and the only reactions come from bot snags and breaker trips.
findings.fix: Shorten thin-3, the loose spare, to about 16 m so it overstretches within the corridor, or give Supply A a short 14 m 'tester' lead whose overstretch zone covers the corridor benches (x −5..0, z 8–9). Port the strain proximity alarm to Lunch: in lunch-runtime render, for each held cable with strain >0.85, alarm along its points at radius 2.2 every 0.7 s, as src/game.ts:301 does. Add a Lunch bonus such as 'Fling the lunch queue's trays' to give the slingshot a target (DR-10).
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/chaos.mjs lunch. With the shortened lead, strain must exceed 1.02 in the corridor, Q must give fastestProp >2 and alarmed ≥2, and world-reacts-15 must show bubbles on the bench blobs.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code. The cables are 32/30/32/30 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61) in a 33×20 m room (src/levels/lunch.ts:15, not 32). release() only slingshots at energy>1 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:199-201). The taut-cable proximity alarm lives in drawCable (src/game.ts:301), which runs only when !this.lunch (src/game.ts:431), so Lunch's cables never alarm anyone. Screenshot world-reacts-14 shows a straight cable with the strain meter short of the limit. I did not reproduce 'can never' myself: wrapping the lead around the kitchen wall could reach overstretch. I lowered it to P2 because the cable still works as a puzzle object in Lunch and the slingshot is available in the other rooms.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:431 (lunch.render replaces drawCable, so no strain alarm)
findings.fix_correction: Shortening thin-3 only matters if the job never needs it to reach far. Check that tests/lunch*.spec routes don't plug thin-3 at long range before you cut it to 16 m. Adding a separate short spare lead is the safer choice.

findings.title: The cable passes straight through coworkers, and they don't notice
findings.problem: Coworkers are not rope obstacles. The rope wraps only around `this.obstacles` plus furniture (src/game.ts:280), and npcs are never added. Dragging the Playground plug from spawn to (−6.3,−5.6) runs the cable straight through the teal trainee at (−6.6,−3.4): 0 bends, strain 0.53, alarmed 0 (world-reacts-24). The hose enters the blob's base and comes out behind it. Pip's own lack of collision with blobs is already reported. This is the cable side of the same problem, and it is a missed gag: in a Good Job–style game, the star object snagging a coworker's legs is the obvious joke, and the clean player would trigger it for free on the way to the socket. A blob can also never 'block the job' or 'help' it, since nothing ties the two systems together.
findings.fix: Add each npc as a round rope obstacle (radius 0.45 at the blob centre) in the obstacle list built at src/game.ts:280, so the cable wraps around blobs. When a rope segment is within 0.5 m of a blob and strain >0.3, set npc.alarm=1 and play a 'hop' (body.position.y += .25 for 0.2 s). At strain >0.95, tip the blob 20° in the direction of the pull. Seated blobs only wobble.
findings.verify: Rerun blobcable.mjs. Expect snap().rope.bends ≥1 around the trainee, alarmed ≥1 within 0.5 s of contact, and world-reacts-24 to show the cable bending around the blob with the '!' bubble.
findings.verify_reason: The rope obstacles are this.obstacles plus prop furniture only (src/game.ts:280). Npcs are never added. I reproduced the drag: picked up the plug and walked to (-6.3,-5.2) past the trainee at (-6.6,-3.4). Result: bends 0, strain 0.53, alarmed 0, and the cable visibly runs into the teal blob's base.
extra_evidence: v.mjs pgcable log: bends 0 strain 0.53 alarmed 0
findings.fix_correction: Rope obstacles are AABBs (minX/maxX/minZ/maxZ) with corner wrapping, not circles, so add each standing npc as a 0.9×0.9 m box. Skip seated npcs, or the Meeting pods become cable mazes. Do not alarm on every contact at strain>0.3 every frame: throttle it to once per 0.7 s, as drawCable does.

findings.title: The startle is a 1-second blip with one pose: it faces Pip rather than the crash, leaves no aftermath, and never escalates
findings.problem: `alarm()` sets npc.alarm=1 (src/game.ts:137), and it decays at 1/s (src/game.ts:423). The bubble pops in over 0.12 s and is gone after exactly 1 s. In every room I tested (playground, lobby, meeting, lunch, qfn, arcade), alarmed was 0 again at +3.5 s, and the coworker had returned to its exact rest pose (world-reacts-01-…-calm, -05-…-calm). The DR-04 timing passes (bubble within 0.5 s), but the reaction is thin. The startled blob turns toward Pip (`watch` → yaw to p, src/game.ts:424), not toward the bin that landed beside it. It doesn't hop, flinch away or glare, and there is no memory: throwing a second bin at the same coworker gives the same 1 s blip. With only one voice per 0.5 s across the whole room (src/game.ts:138), eight blobs startled by one plant make a single chirp. At the game camera, a 1 s bubble on one of 26 blobs is easy to miss while the player is watching the flying prop.
findings.fix: Raise the alarm duration to 1.6 s. Store the impact point on the npc, look at it for the first 0.5 s, then turn and glare at Pip. Add an onset hop (+0.25 m over 0.15 s) and a 0.3 m lean away from the impact. Keep a per-npc `grudge` counter that decays over 20 s: at 2 or more hits, show a 'grumpy' mood face for 6 s, and at 3 or more, have the blob shuffle 1 m away from Pip. Play a second, lower voice for each extra 3 startled blobs. Optionally, add a 'Startle 5 coworkers' bonus to tie reactions to grading (DR-10).
findings.verify: Rerun throw.mjs for playground and meeting. At +0.5 s the screenshot shows the blob facing the impact; at +1.2 s the bubble is still visible; at +3.5 s a twice-hit blob shows the grumpy face.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code. alarm sets npc.alarm=1 (src/game.ts:137), and it decays by render dt (src/game.ts:423), so it lasts 1 s of real time. watch turns the npc's yaw toward Pip's position p, not the impact (src/game.ts:424). There is one global voice per 0.5 s (src/game.ts:138) and no memory per npc. The finding's '+3.5 s calm' measurement is weak evidence, because in manual mode the decay runs on wall-clock time (src/game.ts:454-459). The code alone establishes the 1 s value.

findings.title: Adjacent coworkers' '!' bubbles stack on top of each other
findings.problem: Each bubble is a 0.7 m sprite at y 1.55 (+0.35 when seated), drawn with depthTest false at renderOrder 9 (src/game.ts:132). Boardroom chairs are 1.05 m apart (src/levels/meeting.ts:30), so from the game camera's pitch, one blob's bubble draws straight on top of the bubble of the blob behind it, and the two read as a column of '!' marks (world-reacts-26 crop of world-reacts-17). In the Meeting desk pods, eight bubbles from one plant throw form a dense band (world-reacts-03). The front bubbles also hide the startled faces of the blobs behind them, which are the actual reaction.
findings.fix: Show the bubble only on the 3 blobs nearest the impact; the others get sweat and the startled face only. Offset each bubble sideways by ±0.22 m (screen-right, from the npc seed) and scale seated bubbles to 0.55. Alternatively, project the shown bubbles each frame and nudge any pair closer than 40 px.
findings.verify: Retake the Meeting glass throw (chaos.mjs meeting). In world-reacts-17 no two bubbles overlap, and the green and orange boardroom faces are visible.
findings.verify_reason: Each bubble is a 0.7 m sprite with depthTest false and renderOrder 9 (src/game.ts:132). My own Meeting sprint shot shows two vertical pairs of '!' bubbles stacked over the boardroom blobs, the same as the cited crop.

findings.title: The impact's own dust cloud covers the startled coworker
findings.room: playground (any room where a prop lands beside a blob)
findings.problem: Every counted impact emits `burst(pos,'#e1d4b7',3)` plus three 'dust' puffs (src/game.ts:335). When a flung crate landed beside the trainee after the slingshot, the puffs rendered as three large outlined white balls that covered the trainee's startled face and hands. Only the bubble stayed readable (world-reacts-13, crop world-reacts-27). The effect meant to sell the impact hides the reaction it causes. The sprint-dust sphere issue is already reported; this is the impact burst landing on the reacting blob.
findings.fix: Spawn the impact dust at floor height (y .1), at 40% of the current size, with no outline, and push it 0.5 m away from any npc within 1 m of the impact point. Fade it out over 0.35 s (DR-79).
findings.verify: Rerun chaos.mjs playground and look at world-reacts-13: the trainee's alarm face is fully visible beside the dust.
findings.verify_reason: The impact branch emits burst(pos,'#e1d4b7',3) plus three 'dust' puffs at the impact point (src/game.ts:335). In crop 27, large outlined dust balls cover half of the startled blob, which is the yellow headset blob, not the teal 'trainee' the finding names. My bin throw (verify-02) also shows dust at the blob's base, which was less severe from that angle. It is real, but it depends on the angle.

findings.title: The slingshot startles people around Pip's hand, not where the cable whips and the props fly
findings.problem: `slingshot()` calls `this.alarm(this.plugPosition,6)` (src/game.ts:256), centred on the plug in Pip's hand. In the Playground slingshot (Pip at the end of an overstretched cable, Q), alarmed was 0 at +0.5 s, even though crates were flung across the room (fastestProp 6.8, damage 1). The trainee next to the flying crates only startled 3 s later, when a crate landed beside it (world-reacts-12 vs -13). The biggest chaos act in the game gets no instant audience reaction. The whip happens along the cable, where the props are, often more than 6 m from the hand.
findings.fix: In slingshot(), call `this.alarm(mid,3)` for each rope segment midpoint (as the strain alarm does at src/game.ts:301), plus the existing alarm at the hand. In the same loop, alarm any npc within 2 m of each flung prop's start position.
findings.verify: Rerun chaos.mjs playground. At +0.5 s after Q, alarmed ≥1, with the trainee by the crate row showing a bubble in world-reacts-12.
findings.verify_reason: The code is as described: slingshot alarms only at plugPosition with radius 6 (src/game.ts:256), so blobs beside props flung far from the hand react only when the props land. My reproduction contradicts the observation, though. I ran the same Playground slingshot (strain 1.04, Q) and got alarmed=1 at +0.1 s and damage 2. The 'alarmed 0 at +0.5 s' result is not robust. The underlying design point (props whipped far along the cable get no audience) still stands from the code.

findings.title: Throwing paper, the commonest prop next to Pip, does nothing at all
findings.problem: In the Garage and Spectrum, the nearest prop to Pip on the way to the coworker was a paper sheet (0.56 m and 0.57 m). After E then Q, nothing happens: there is no impact, alarmed stays 0 and damage stays 0 (world-reacts-06, -09). Paper drag (src/game.ts:337) keeps it below the 5.5 m/s impact threshold, so it drifts down at Pip's feet. The Observatory box throw also produced no impact or reaction (world-reacts-08). In practice the player's first experiment ('what if I throw this?') often gets the dullest possible answer, and the coworker four metres away doesn't react.
findings.fix: Treat a paper throw as a flutter gag. On Q, split the sheet into a 6-sheet burst using the existing 'paper' kind and the flutter physics. When any sheet passes within 1.2 m of a blob's head, set alarm=.6 with no damage. Alternatively, make the clutter recipes place paper as stacks of 5 (one prop that bursts on landing).
findings.verify: Rerun throw.mjs garage and spectrum. After Q there are visible fluttering sheets and alarmed ≥1 if a blob is within 1.5 m of the flight path, with damage 0.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it in the Playground: my first run grabbed a paper sheet (the nearest prop), and after Q fastestProp peaked at 5.0, then 2–2.6. It never hit the lastSpeed>5.5 / Δ>3.5 impact test (src/game.ts:335), and alarmed, damage and cost all stayed 0 for 3 s. Paper drag at src/game.ts:337 explains why. The 'nearest prop is paper' claims for Garage, Spectrum and Observatory were not re-run.
extra_evidence: v.mjs pg first run (held paper): timeline all alarmed 0, dmg 0

findings.title: Plug-in and switch sparks never startle or cheer anyone
findings.problem: DR-04 counts sparks as triggers, but the two sparks every clean player makes don't involve coworkers. plugFlash() emits sparks, a flash, a ring and stars but never calls alarm (src/game.ts:249). The lamp or projector switch spark (src/game.ts:217) doesn't either. Only breaker trips and Lunch snags and shorts alarm (src/meeting-strip.ts:82, src/lunch-runtime.ts:260-264). In the Lunch clean run, the kitchen plug spark at 33.9 s happens with the chef watching from the oven, and nobody reacts (world-reacts-21: the chef faces Pip, no bubble). The 'something happened' beat that would land on the clean route (finding: no moment in 30 s) is wasted.
findings.fix: In plugFlash(), give coworkers within 5 m a short positive reaction: set a new `npc.cheerT=.8` (a bounce like the win cheer, src/game.ts:426) and play voice('cheer') at most once per 0.5 s. Switch sparks call alarm(at,1.5), so a blob standing at the switch flinches.
findings.verify: Rerun clean.mjs lunch. At the PLUG row, the chef bounces and a cheer voice plays. In the Playground, a trainee placed within 5 m of the socket bounces in the plug screenshot.
findings.verify_reason: plugFlash (src/game.ts:249) and the switch spark (src/game.ts:217) never call alarm or any npc reaction. Only the breaker trip (src/meeting-strip.ts:82) and Lunch's snag/trip/short (src/lunch-runtime.ts:260-264) do. DR-04 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:63) explicitly lists sparks as triggers, so this is a rule gap, not just polish.

findings.title: Coworkers never move, so the world never causes chaos by itself, and chaos can never help or block the job
findings.problem: The npc update only changes rotation, scale and body offset (src/game.ts:423-430), never `group.position`. Every coworker is a fixed statue. A blob walking into the cable or the plug, knocking a prop into the route, or wandering through a doorway can't happen. The only autonomous agents in any floor room are Lunch's cleaner bots, which do interact with cables (snag, src/lunch-runtime.ts:260; world-reacts-14 shows a bot about to cross the live lead). So in the Playground, Meeting and lobby, DR-03's 'without the player looking for it' has no source except the player. Neither 'chaos helps' nor 'chaos blocks' is ever caused by a coworker.
findings.fix: Give one coworker per floor room a short patrol: a coffee run (Meeting: desk pod → coffee corner at (−12.7,4.5)); a trainee pacing the practice wall (Playground). Move them at 1.2 m/s with the existing breathe bob. When the patrol crosses a rope segment and strain >0.4, they trip: tilt 70°, alarm, and a 0.3 m nudge to the cable. Keep the patrol path out of the clean lanes, so it adds comedy without blocking (DR-16).
findings.verify: In the Meeting start shot plus 15 s of advance(), the patrolling blob is visibly elsewhere. Dragging the cable across its path produces a trip pose with a bubble.
findings.verify_reason: The npc loop (src/game.ts:423-430) only writes group.rotation.y, body.scale, body.position.y and body.rotation.z. group.position is set once in addNpc (src/game.ts:133) and never again. Lunch's bots are the only moving agents, and they do snag cables (src/lunch-runtime.ts:260).
findings.fix_correction: Also make sure a patrolling blob is added to audit() (src/game.ts:498, standing coworkers) and the respawn logic. A trip that nudges the cable must never unplug a connected lead in the clean solution, or it would break 'never fail for chaos'.

findings.title: In Lunch, E picks up cable ends before props, so Pip can't grab the boxes beside his spawn
findings.problem: Lunch's interact() runs before the generic grab (src/game.ts:200). Its last branch takes any cable end within 1.75 m for E as well as F (src/lunch-runtime.ts:172). The power room has four cable ends lying around Pip's spawn, so walking up to the boxes at (−11.5,8.3) and (−12.8,8.5) and pressing E never grabs a box: snap().held stays undefined, because E picks up a cable end instead and the next E drops it (mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/lunchprobe.mjs log). The third E grabbed the thick dolly, a job item. The throw test in the power room failed for the same reason (world-reacts-04, prompt 'F Pick up the thin cable end'). This breaks DR-22: E is grab, F is plug. In the first seconds of the room, the player's first 'grab something' produces an invisible cable pick-up instead of a prop in hand.
findings.fix: In LunchRuntime.interact, take the cable-end branch only when cableOnly is true (F). With E, fall through to the generic prop grab unless no prop is within 1.65 m.
findings.verify: Rerun lunchprobe.mjs. Pressing E at (−11.08,7.42) gives snap().held==='box' and lunch.held stays null; F at the same spot still picks up the thin cable.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. At the box nearest spawn, Pip stands at (-11.11,7.49) and the prompt reads 'F Pick up the thin cable end', not a grab prompt. Pressing E gives held undefined and lunch.held {thin-3, end 1}, holdingPlug true. Cause: game.interact calls lunch.interact(cableOnly) first (src/game.ts:200), and with cableOnly=false that path falls through to the cable-end branch (src/lunch-runtime.ts:172). The box is never offered.
extra_evidence: v.mjs lunch log: after E held undefined, lunch.held thin-3
findings.fix_correction: Also update LunchRuntime.promptAt (src/lunch-runtime.ts:186-187) so the E grab prompt shows when a prop is in reach. Check that tests/lunch*.spec and tools/debug/bench-lunch do not rely on E for picking up cables before you change it.

findings.title: The DR-03 'fastestProp' signal counts the prop in Pip's hands, so the funny-moment check passes on a plain pick-up
findings.problem: snapshot().fastestProp (src/game.ts:504) is the maximum linear speed over all props, including `this.held`. The carry code drives the held prop with `setLinvel(… *12)` (src/game.ts:331), so it reads 5–7 m/s whenever Pip walks with something. In the Meeting clean run, the log shows fast=5.1 at 1.3 s, just from lifting the power strip, and 6.1–6.9 while carrying the coupler and extension. Nothing funny happened, but the DR-03 check ('fastestProp > 5 before 30 s') passes. Any automated fun check built on this field gives false passes.
findings.fix: Exclude `this.held` and the dolly/cart Pip is pushing from fastestProp. Also add a `snapshot().beats` array that pushes {t,kind:'impact'|'break'|'spark'|'confetti'|'alarm'|'slingshot'} at each existing burst() or alarm() call site, so specs can assert DR-03 directly.
findings.verify: Rerun clean.mjs meeting. The fast column stays <1 while carrying the strip, and `beats` lists the strip ring, the first alarm (about 64 s) and the trip spark.
findings.verify_reason: In code, snapshot().fastestProp maps over every prop, including this.held (src/game.ts:504), and the held prop is driven by setLinvel(…×12) (src/game.ts:331). The magnitude did not reproduce: lifting the Meeting strip peaked at 3.42, and carrying it read 1.5–2.0, not 5.1–6.9. No test asserts DR-03 with fastestProp. The only use is tests/routes.spec.ts:58, after a slingshot with nothing held, so there are no current false passes. It is a tooling trap, not a player-facing issue.
extra_evidence: v.mjs meetstrip log: fast while carrying [3.42,1.85,1.76,1.71,1.46,1.96]

notes.fun: DR-04 timing passes in every room I tested. A thrown prop that counts as an impact puts the '!' bubble, sweat and startled face on coworkers within 4.5 m in under 0.5 s: Playground trainee (0.24 m from the bin), Lobby receptionist (chair onto the desk), Meeting (one plant startles 8 pod workers, a nice comic ripple), Lunch corridor queue (2), QFN (1), Arcade (2). Everyone is calm again by +3.5 s, with no lingering bubbles. Three rooms got no reaction from the nearest throwable: Garage and Spectrum (paper), Observatory (box). Where the system falls short: (1) reactions are tied to the damage counter, so play is billed as breakage; (2) it is a 1 s blip that faces Pip; (3) nothing reacts to the clean player, and no clean route reaches a physical or funny beat inside 30 s (Playground has only the 8.6 s plug flash, Meeting's first alarm is at 64 s, Lunch's first spark at 33.9 s); (4) the big set pieces don't fire. Meeting glass can't be smashed and slides open for free; Lunch can't be slingshot near its crowd; the Playground slingshot alarm is centred on the hand, not the whip. Lunch's bots are the one autonomous comedy source, and they interact with the cable as designed.
notes.playability: Chaos never blocked the job in my runs. Coworkers never move, have no colliders and are not rope obstacles, so they can neither block nor help. Chaos helps in one unintended way: sprinting into a Meeting glass pane slides it 1.1 m and opens a free shortcut into the boardroom. In Lunch, E grabs cable ends ahead of props in the cable-dense power room. The stepped clean-route walker in Meeting stalled at x≈8 with the 37.2 m chain (14 s at a strain alarm, then F released the plug at the pane). That walker differs from the spec's straight walk, so I didn't file it, but routing past the glass panes looks fragile. Zero console errors in every run.
notes.teaching: Not a teaching pass. One note: plug-in sparks (the moment the loop closes) get no audience response, so the world doesn't mark the electrical 'aha' the way it marks a tossed bin.
notes.clarity: At the game camera the bubbles are big and readable: about 40 px, depthTest off, and on screen even at the frame edge (Playground trainee at the bottom-right). Two clarity problems: adjacent seated coworkers' bubbles stack into a column, and the impact dust hides the startled face. The HUD damage and cost jump with no visible broken state on the prop, so the player can't tell what they 'broke'.
notes.models: The startled blob variant (a wide eye, the 'o' mouth, and the hands up via the arm capsule rotated −2.3) reads well up close (world-reacts-24 area, world-reacts-27). The pose change is mainly a squash to 0.72, which is subtle at zoom 26–36 next to the bubble. A hop or lean would carry the reaction at the game camera.
